title: CEO Interview with Vera Yang of Flexcompute
gist: Flexcompute president Vera Yang says the bottleneck in AI-assisted chip design has shifted from generating designs to verifying them, and pitches its 'Tokenized Physics' Physics World Model (neural nets fused with first-principles solvers) as an agent-native verification layer. Key data: 250+ customer companies, October investment from Samsung Ventures and Applied Ventures, five agents rebuilt 34 photonic circuits that all passed DRC/LVS, and a warpage twin covering 800,000+ solder points.

insights.claim: Flexcompute had five AI agents rebuild photonic circuits from published papers; they built 34 so far, including a 32x32 switch with 1,024 Mach-Zehnder interferometers, and every one passed DRC and LVS.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agents can already generate manufacturable photonic layouts, commoditizing design generation.
insights.quote: Every one passed DRC and LVS.

insights.claim: Vera Yang argues the hard part of AI-driven chip design is shifting from generating options to knowing which ones will work: capturing design intent, simulating the full circuit, and closing the loop with measured data.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value in AI-EDA may accrue to verification/simulation layers rather than generative design tools.
insights.quote: So the hard part is shifting from generating options to knowing which ones will work
insights.locator: So the hard part is shifting

insights.claim: As engineering teams bring agents into the flow, the key question becomes whether an agent-proposed design can be trusted enough to send to the fab.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Trust/verification becomes a gating factor for agentic chip design adoption.
insights.quote: if an agent proposes a design, can we trust it enough to send it to the fab?

insights.claim: Flexcompute contends that AI surrogate models trained on past simulation data are only as good as their data and can be confidently wrong on novel designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to surrogate-model AI startups competing in simulation.
insights.quote: Surrogates are only as good as their data and can be confidently wrong on a design no one has seen before.
insights.locator: There are established simulation and EDA vendors

insights.claim: Flexcompute's Tokenized Physics builds neural networks and physics solvers into one model, which it says makes validated solvers fast enough to run inside AI-driven design loops.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Physics-grounded AI is a distinct architectural bet versus pure data-driven surrogates.
insights.locator: Flexcompute is a frontier AI lab

insights.claim: Flexcompute's photonics customers include AMD, Anduril, Nvidia, Samsung Display, Coherent, TDK, Ayar Labs and GlobalFoundries, and optical I/O and co-packaged optics for AI data centers are its fastest-growing work.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals strong design activity in co-packaged optics for AI data centers.
insights.quote: Optical I/O and co-packaged optics for AI data centers are the fastest-growing part of that work.

insights.claim: In a full optical I/O chip with eight 100 Gb/s wavelength channels, demultiplexer filters with about -18 dB crosstalk looked fine individually but, simulated as a full link, the leakage added up and noticeably degraded the eye.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: System-level simulation catches failures that component datasheets miss, supporting demand for full-chip photonic simulation.
insights.quote: You only see that when the whole chip is simulated together.

insights.claim: A photonic chip or advanced package that fails after tapeout costs months and millions of dollars, and the stakes rise as optics move closer to the processor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising respin cost justifies higher spending on pre-tapeout simulation.

insights.claim: Flexcompute released PhotonForge 2.0 in October so engineers and agents work on one design from PDK and schematic through layout, multi-physics simulation, DRC, LVS and tapeout, with physics-verified compact models and automatic Verilog-A export.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agent-native EDA tooling is emerging as a product category.

insights.claim: As chiplets, HBM and optics share one package, heat, stress, warpage and reliability effects interact, creating system-level simulation problems that were previously too large or slow to solve.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous integration expands the multiphysics simulation TAM.
insights.locator: We're also strong in the physics

insights.claim: Flexcompute's warpage Physics Twin predicts which of more than 800,000 solder points will fail under heat before a design goes to production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Warpage/solder reliability is a material risk in large AI packages.
insights.quote: predicts which of more than 800,000 solder points will fail under heat before the design goes to production
insights.locator: We're also strong in the physics

insights.claim: Flexcompute plans to extend physics verification of AI-assisted designs into industry-standard EDA flows and expand Physics Twins for advanced packaging starting with warpage, thermal and signal integrity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Possible partnership or competitive overlap with incumbent EDA vendors.

insights.claim: More than 250 companies across semiconductors, photonics, aerospace, automotive and defense use Flexcompute's technology, built by a team of more than 70 PhDs founded out of Stanford and MIT.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Indicates meaningful commercial traction for a physics-AI simulation startup.

insights.claim: Samsung Ventures and Applied Ventures invested in Flexcompute in October 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Strategic investment from Samsung and Applied Materials' venture arms signals interest in physics-AI for chips and packaging.
insights.quote: In October, Samsung Ventures and Applied Ventures invested in Flexcompute.

insights.claim: Flexcompute uses a product-led funnel: free PhotonForge Community runs locally and agents can start using it from docs, with Enterprise adding foundry PDK integration, EDA connectors, version control and traceability.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agent-accessible free tiers could be a new go-to-market model in EDA.
insights.locator: Most teams start with PhotonForge Community
